In summary, our research is concerned with
the net-baryon number fluctuations, which is a sensitive probe to search for the phase transition between QGP and hadronic matter.
the net-proton cumulants at RHIC energies and their possible baselines, and the net-baryon cumulants in AMPT model.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the net-proton and net-baryon cumulants are observed to be consistent with the Poisson baseline at s NN =19.6 and27 GeV, but deviate from the Poisson and binomial baseline at s NN ≥ 39 GeV.

the net-proton cumulants at 19.7 GeV are consistent with the Poisson baseline, while the net-proton and net-baryon cumulants are consistent with the Binomial baseline at 27 GeV and the net-proton data deviate from both baselines at 39 and 200 GeV.
the net-proton data deviates from the Poisson and the Binomial baselines at 19.7 and 27 Gev, but the data is not conclusive enough to say that there is a clear signal for the QCD critical point.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the net-baryon cumulants at 19. 6 GeV in the UrQMD model, and the net-proton cumulants at all energies in the UrQCD, AMPT and Binomial baseline are compatible with each other.
the net-proton cumulants at RHIC energies are consistent with a non-trivial baseline, but the net-baryon cumulants at the top RHIC energies are still dominated by the trivial baseline.

the net-proton cumulant ratios for 0–10% central collisions in the 19.6–200 GeV energy range can be well explained by the UrQMD model, while the AMPT model is able to explain the 19.4–200 GeV data, but fails at 7.7 GeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
net-proton cumulant data deviate from the baseline measures and are consistent with the UrQMD and the AMPT model predictions at 19.7 GeV and 27 Gev.
the net-proton and net-baryon cumulant data are in good agreement with the UrQMD model at 19.4 GeV, while they are in good agreement in the AMPT model at 27 GeV.
the net-proton cumulants at 19.7 and 27 Gev show significant deviation from the baseline measures.
